title: Three Atlanta Indian Americans Featured Among 70 Global Achievers in 'Jewels of India'
excerpt: Emory scholar Jagdish Sheth, community leader Madhu Sheth and physician-turned-banker Neel Neelagaru are profiled in Maneesh Media's coffee-table book covering 70 Indians across 11 countries.
body:
• Three Atlanta-area Indian Americans — Dr Jagdish Sheth, Madhuri "Madhu" Sheth and Dr Narasimhulu "Neel" Neelagaru — are featured in Jewels of India – Bharat ki Shaan, Bharat ka Abhiman.
  • The Maneesh Media coffee-table book profiles 70 Indians across 11 countries, including the US, Canada and the UAE, and was launched on February 18, 2026 at The Ashok Hotel in New Delhi by Union Culture and Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat.
  • Jagdish Sheth is Emory University's Charles H. Kellstadt Professor of Marketing, a Padma Bhushan awardee with more than 300 papers and 30 books; Madhu Sheth is a former first female president of the Jain Society of Greater Atlanta.
  • Neelagaru, a cardiologist, founded Quantum National Bank in 1995 and grew its assets from about $5 million to $665 million before its 2023 merger into HomeTrust Bancshares.

Three prominent Indian Americans from the Atlanta area are featured in Jewels of India – Bharat ki Shaan, Bharat ka Abhiman, a coffee-table book celebrating the achievements of 70 Indians across 11 countries, NRI Pulse reported. The three are marketing scholar Dr Jagdish Sheth, community leader and philanthropist Madhuri "Madhu" Sheth, and physician-turned-banker Dr Narasimhulu "Neel" Neelagaru.

The book, published by Maneesh Media, was launched by Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Gajendra Singh Shekhawat on February 18, 2026, at The Ashok Hotel in New Delhi, according to both NRI Pulse and Maneesh Media. Its profiles cover entrepreneurs, business leaders, doctors, scientists, academics and community builders in countries including the United States, Canada and the United Arab Emirates. Maneesh Media, headquartered in Jaipur with a presence in New York and Toronto, has spent more than two decades documenting diaspora achievers; the book's cover incorporates a waveform representing the spoken word "Bharat."

Jagdish Sheth: the scholar

Jagdish Sheth is the Charles H. Kellstadt Professor of Marketing at Emory University's Goizueta Business School, which he joined in 1991 after posts at Columbia, MIT, the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign and USC. Born in Yangon in 1938, he arrived in the United States in 1961. He has published more than 300 scholarly papers and over 30 books, and is known for developing the Howard-Sheth Theory of Buyer Behavior with his mentor John Howard. India honoured him with the Padma Bhushan in 2020 for contributions to literature and education. Through the Sheth Foundation and Sheth Family Foundation, he and his wife support research, scholarships and cultural programs in India and the US.

Madhu Sheth: the community builder

Madhu Sheth, born in Kutch, Gujarat and raised in Chennai, is recognised for community leadership and preservation of Jain heritage. She was a driving force behind the Jain Society of Greater Atlanta, its first female president, and holds leadership roles in JAINA, the Federation of Jain Associations in North America. Her profile recalls arriving in the US in the early 1960s, when Indian groceries, temples and community networks were scarce, and her years teaching Indian languages and vegetarian cooking as the family moved across the country.

Neel Neelagaru: from village school to bank board

Neelagaru was born in 1949 in Ballari, Karnataka, and attended a village school that lacked electricity and classrooms. He graduated in medicine as valedictorian, arrived in New York in 1973, built a cardiology practice, and served as chief of staff at BJC Medical Center after moving to Georgia. In 1995, while still practising medicine, he founded Quantum Capital Corporation and Quantum National Bank; by its 2023 merger with HomeTrust Bancshares, the bank's assets had grown from about $5 million to $665 million, according to his profile. He continues to serve on the HomeTrust boards and as a commissioner on the Georgia Student Finance Commission, and his philanthropy covers scholarships, nursing education, libraries and free medical services.

The book and individual profiles are available on the Maneesh Media website.
